newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa taken to hospital with heart trouble.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa taken to hospital with heart trouble.

text.p: Mother Teresa was taken to hospital with heart trouble on Friday, the third time since August that she has been admitted for emergency care, a doctor treating the Roman Catholic missionary said.

"She had some cardiac problems and we have decided to admit her," the doctor at Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta told Reuters. He said the hospital would release a statement on her condition later in the day.
The 86-year-old nun spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands Nursing Home in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
Two weeks after she returned to her Missionaries of Charity religious order, the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner fell off a chair and hit her head.
A brain scan revealed a blood clot in her brain but it disappeared and she was later released.

Mother Teresa's health began to deteriorate in 1989 when she was fitted with a heart pacemaker. Since then she has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria, lung problems and heart disease.
